title: One Fits All: Learning Fair Graph Neural Networks for Various Sensitive Attributes

problem.claim: Graph neural networks can produce discriminatory predictions against protected groups defined by sensitive attributes.

gap.claim: Existing graph fairness approaches are often tailored to specific sensitive attributes, requiring retraining from scratch when the sensitive-attribute requirement changes and incurring high computational costs.

contributions.claim: The fairness problem in graphs is analyzed from a causal modeling perspective by identifying the sensitive attribute's confounding effect as an underlying reason for unfairness.
FairINV is proposed as an invariant-learning graph fairness framework for training fair graph neural networks that accommodate various sensitive attributes within a single training session.
FairINV uses sensitive-attribute partition and eliminates spurious correlations between labels and various sensitive attributes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on several real-world datasets reportedly show that FairINV significantly outperforms state-of-the-art fairness approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks may generate discriminatory predictions against protected groups.
Existing methods are sensitive-attribute-specific and require costly retraining when requirements change.
The issue is framed causally through confounding induced by sensitive attributes and through invariant learning across environments.
FairINV trains fair graph neural networks for multiple sensitive attributes in a single session using partitioning and spurious-correlation elimination.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show improvements over state-of-the-art fairness approaches.

source_observation.claim: Methods specialized to one sensitive attribute may require retraining when the required sensitive attribute changes.

interpretation.claim: Separating invariant information from sensitive-attribute-specific confounding may support reuse across multiple fairness requirements.

application.claim: When fairness requirements may vary, consider training representations designed to remain invariant across sensitive-attribute environments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that invariant learning will generalize to sensitive attributes, datasets, or settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, fairness metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the sensitive-attribute partitioning procedure or the optimization objective.
The abstract does not establish performance under sensitive attributes or settings outside the reported experiments.
